title: Held On, Hauled In
theme: Alex Baker limped home to the TEG 18 Trophy with the worst gross card in the field while Gregg Williams played the round of the week to seal the Green Jacket, the Stadium's closing four holes doing damage to almost everyone.
opening_hook: Three of the five men in the field walked off the Stadium's 14th having taken at least six shots; one of them won the Trophy anyway.

round_story.subject: Gregg Williams's 44-point, 84-gross closing round at the Stadium — the best round of the day by two points and the card that sealed the TEG 18 Green Jacket by 14
round_story.why_it_matters: It was the best Stableford round of the day (44, against John Patterson's 42, Alex Baker's and David Mullin's 38 and Jon Baker's 29), the lowest gross of the day at 12 over par, a new personal best for Williams at PGA Catalunya - Stadium on his seventh visit there — 84, one better than the 85 he had posted on the same course earlier this TEG — and his third-best gross round in 67 TEG rounds. It also turned an eight-shot Green Jacket lead into a 14-shot win.
round_story.shape: Setup: Williams arrived at the Stadium eight clear of David Mullin in the Green Jacket and nine points adrift of Alex Baker in the Trophy, having trailed the Trophy by 15 at one point. Turn: a birdie at the par-three 5th began a spell of clean golf, and nine Stableford points across the 8th, 9th and 10th — par, bogey at stroke index one, par — took him through the turn without giving anything back. Resolution: 84 gross, a course personal best, the Jacket won by 14 over David Mullin, and the Trophy closed to nine with nowhere left to close it.
headline_candidates: Williams Signs Off With a Stadium Best
Forty-Four Points and a Green Jacket
Williams Saves His Best For Last
round_story.chosen_headline: Williams Signs Off With a Stadium Best
round_story.standfirst: His 84 bettered by one the mark he had set on the same course earlier in the week, and stands as the third-best gross round of his 67 in TEG competition.

race_story.subject: Alex Baker wins the TEG 18 Trophy by eight from John Patterson while signing for 36 over par, a ten and an eight, and finishing last of five in the Green Jacket
race_story.why_it_matters: This is the tournament's resolution: Alex Baker takes the TEG 18 Trophy on 169 from John Patterson's 161, Gregg Williams takes the TEG 18 Green Jacket on 66 from David Mullin's 80, and Jon Baker takes the TEG 18 Wooden Spoon on 126, 23 behind David Mullin. The comedy is in how the Trophy was collected: the champion's 38 points were joint third of five on the day, his 36 over par was the worst gross card in the field by 11 shots, and his 12-point overnight cushion was cut to eight without ever being genuinely threatened.
race_story.shape: Setup: Alex Baker began the Stadium 12 points clear, with John Patterson the only man with the arithmetic to reach him. Turn: Patterson took nine points from the 4th, 5th and 6th and Alex Baker bled seven shots across the 9th, 10th and 11th, then took ten at the par-four 14th and eight at the 17th, and still the lead never fell below eight. Resolution: 169 to 161 for the Trophy, with the champion 124 over par for the week in the Green Jacket — last of the five — and both Jacket and Spoon settled by margins nobody was going to argue with.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Wins While Going Backwards
A Ten, an Eight and the Trophy
Eight Points Clear and Falling Apart
race_story.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Wins While Going Backwards
race_story.standfirst: John Patterson posted the better card on two of the four days and still finished eight behind, which is the whole tournament in one sentence.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker's 29-point closing round — five consecutive double bogeys from the 7th to the 11th — completes a Wooden Spoon taken by 23 shots
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He was last in the field in three of the four rounds, never posted the best round of the day, and finished 23 points behind David Mullin, the next worst. The 29 was the lowest round of the day by nine points, and the middle of it is almost geometric: double bogey, double bogey, double bogey, double bogey, double bogey.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: already 14 adrift of the Spoon before a ball was struck, Jon Baker needed only to avoid the spectacular. Turn: from the 7th to the 11th he made five straight double bogeys, ten shots gone in five holes, one Stableford point apiece, before a birdie at the 13th finally broke an eleven-hole run without a hole in par or better. Resolution: 29 points, 97 gross, last again, and the TEG 18 Wooden Spoon by 23.
headline_candidates: Jon Baker Takes the Spoon by Twenty-Three
Jon Baker's Metronomic March to the Spoon
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Jon Baker Takes the Spoon by Twenty-Three
discovered_storylines.standfirst: His five consecutive double bogeys from the 7th were the most consistent golf anybody played all afternoon.

discovered_storylines.subject: The Stadium's closing stretch, the 14th to the 17th, as the round's real protagonist — David Mullin nine shots gone in four holes, John Patterson a triple then a double then a rescuing birdie
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Three of the five men took six or worse at the 14th alone, and the four holes from the 14th to the 17th accounted for the day's two ugliest sequences plus the champion's ten and eight. On the seventh TEG round at this venue, the course closed out the tournament more decisively than any player did.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: with the Jacket and Trophy effectively settled, the field turned for home on a course designed as a European Tour championship test. Turn: David Mullin went double, triple, double, double from the 14th, nine shots dropped and not a net par among them; John Patterson took seven at the 14th and seven at the par-five 15th before a birdie at the 17th stopped the bleeding. Resolution: nobody's position changed, and everyone had something to say about the 14th.
headline_candidates: The Stadium Has the Final Word
discovered_storylines.standfirst: David Mullin's four-hole run home cost him nine shots and changed nothing at all, which is the purest form of golf there is.

race_state_note: Gregg Williams finished on 160, nine points off the Trophy, having trailed it by 15 at one stage; John Patterson posted the better round than Alex Baker on two of the four days and still lost by eight. TEG 18 is not a double — Trophy and Jacket went to different men; there have been seven doubles before now (TEGs 2, 4, 11, 13, 14, 15 and 17). Do not cite career win tallies for any player: the supplied counts do not make clear whether TEG 18 is included.
